rationale: Narrowed clause (a) of the recovery-value family fact, which generalised a non-owner recoverer's behaviour to every recovery. The fabricated ballot is the recoverer's own id for the instance owner and id + N for any other recoverer, and while IsLeader is false it never advances; the adoption loop therefore skips genuine replies only when the fabricated ballot sits above them, which is the non-owner case measured by the value-adoption receipt (replies at value ballot 0 passed over against a fabricated ballot of 8), whereas an owner recovering its own instance fabricates its own id, which equals the peers' value ballot in this configuration, so their replies are still adopted - the equality case that clause (d) and the delivery-order receipts rely on. The clause now names both branches, with the ballot rule's own source lines, and no other clause, condition, source or citation changes.

knowledge.statement: In the captured EPaxos package the value a recovery adopts is not protected by the quorum that holds it: four distinct mechanisms of the same recovery path each let a recovering replica end up proposing, and then deciding, a value other than the one its prepare replies carry. (a) startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own state - the recoverer's own id when it is the instance owner and id + N when it is not, without advancing while IsLeader is false - and the adoption loop then honours only replies whose value ballot is at least that fabricated one, so a non-owner recoverer's fabricated ballot sits above the peers' stored value ballots and its genuine replies are skipped (measured: replies at value ballot 0 were passed over against a fabricated ballot of 8), while an owner recovering its own instance fabricates its own id, which equals the peers' value ballot, so their replies are still adopted - the case (d) depends on (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1145-1165, 1239-1246). (b) A reply whose value ballot is below the running candidate ballot - which begins at the recoverer's pre-recovery local value ballot and rises to the fabricated recovery ballot as the loop adopts - is ignored even when it reports the highest accepted value, so a NOOP replaces an accepted value, including one another live replica has already committed; a reply whose value ballot equals the running candidate is still adopted, which is what lets an empty reply replace the command in (d). (c) A reply that reports the instance COMMITTED is discarded once its status reaches lb.status, because the pre-accept guard then rejects the remaining replies, so the first recovery attempt stalls until the retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:870-881, 1255-1313). (d) A reply that carries no command decodes as a non-nil empty slice, which the sub-case 5/6 fallback passes to startPhase1 instead of state.NOOP() (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), and the adopted value is the one carried by the last reply appended before the appended count reaches SlowQuorumSize - the fabricated self reply counts toward that threshold, so the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply and the dispatch then replaces the bookkeeping, so replies delivered afterwards cannot restore the command; the owner's command therefore survives exactly when that second peer reply carries it, measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies as kept for the orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2 and dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2. Recovering replicas that already hold the value are not affected by (a)-(b), and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window and the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, or (for the arrival-order variant) recovers its own instance while replies at the same value ballot differ.

knowledge.assertion: empty slice adopted and passed through, with the reply at the slow-quorum trigger position deciding the command and no later reply able to re-open it
COMMITTED status adopted then later replies discarded
a recovery lacking the command can decide a different value than a live replica's committed value
